 🚨 Alarm: If the AED is removed, an alarm sounds to alert those nearby.
 🌬️ Ventilation fan: Helps keep the cabinet cool and ventilated during those hot summer months.
 🔥 Heating pad: Helps protect the AED from the cold during the winter.
 Having an AED readily accessible in our community could make a lifesaving difference when seconds matter. We’re proud to see this important safety resource added to the Community Center! ❤️
 So… did you find Justin? 👀

items.title: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in the G20 area grew by 0.7% in the second quarter of 2026, slightly down from 0.8% in the...
items.content_text:
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in the G20 area grew by 0.7% in the second quarter of 2026, slightly down from 0.8% in the previous quarter. 
 Among G20 economies, the contraction in Saudi Arabia deepened, with GDP falling by 4.8% in Q2 2026, following a 1.4% decline in Q1, this mainly reflected a sharp decrease in oil activities. 
 By contrast, growth rebounded strongly in Mexico, with GDP increasing by 1.4% in Q2 after contracting by 0.3% in Q1, and remained strong in Indonesia, at 1.3% (similar to Q1). Growth also strengthened in Türkiye, from 0.3% to 1.1%, and in Canada, from 0.1% to 0.8%, while it picked up slightly in Australia, from 0.3% to 0.4%. In France, GDP was unchanged in Q2, following a contraction of 0.2% in Q1.  
 Learn more: https://brnw.ch/21x5Hfv | #OECDstats

Live from NPR’s Tiny Desk: Two Chattanooga artists setting out to make history with their music.  
 Released only a week apart, these two were recently featured on NPR’s coveted music series — a feat accomplished by Chattanooga’s homegrown talent not seen since Usher’s performance in 2022. Here’s a little bit of what NPR had to say:  
 Isaiah Rashad put everything into this Tiny Desk. As a result, the pride of Chattanooga crafts a performance that feels like a debut for longtime fans and newcomers alike.  
 Mon Rovîa’s voice is like a balm: soft, clear, soothing. He uses that voice to tackle difficult, yet poignant vignettes — of battles fought internally and others observed in the world around him.  
 Watch the full performances on Youtube!

🚂 Congratulations to the Tennessee Valley Railroad Museum on 65 years of preservation!
 For more than six decades, the Tennessee Valley Railroad Museum has demonstrated the power of preservation by keeping our region’s railroad history alive and accessible to future generations.
 Chattanooga’s identity and growth are inseparable from its railroad heritage, and TVRM has been an extraordinary steward of that story. Their work is a reminder that preservation is about more than protecting the past, it's about finding ways for history to remain an active and meaningful part of our lives today.
 Congratulations to the staff, volunteers, supporters, and generations of preservationists who have made 65 years possible. Here’s to many more years of keeping Chattanooga’s railroad history on track!

Getting to class can be one of the most routine parts of a student’s day, but the hassle of parking, navigating Chattanooga’s heat and long walks across campus can throw that routine off. For students looking to ease these burdens, UTC offers the Mocs Express shuttle as a convenient, safe way to get around campus free of charge. 🚌 
 The Mocs Express shuttle operates a regular 13-hour route Monday through Friday, with a special Friday evening route for students to enjoy. Starting at Engel Stadium, the Mocs Express runs through campus and the neighboring streets for a complete loop of less than 30 minutes. Once the bus returns to its starting point, the route restarts.
 🔗  Read more here: https://blog.utc.edu/…/your-ride-around-campus-getting-to-…/

items.content_text:
It is with profound sadness that the City of East Ridge announces the passing of Councilman Jacky Cagle.
 For nearly half a century, Jacky dedicated his life to serving the people of East Ridge first as a City employee from 1976 to 2010 and later as a member of the East Ridge City Council from 2014 to 2026.
 Through every chapter of his service, Jacky worked to leave East Ridge stronger and better than he found it.  His dedication to our community, the relationships he built, and the legacy he leaves behind will not be forgotten.
 “We are overwhelmed by the loss of Council Member Jacky Cagle,” said Mayor Brian Williams.  "He was a friend and someone who truly cared about East Ridge and the people who call our community home.
 The City of East Ridge extends its heartfelt thoughts and prayers to his wife, Donna, and their family during this incredibly difficult time.  May they find strength and comfort in knowing how much Jacky meant to so many people and how deeply he will be missed."
 Information regarding arrangements will be shared once it has been finalized and made publicly available by the family.
 A lifetime of service.  A lasting legacy in #EastRidgeTN! 🤍

UTC welcomed 11,809 students for fall 2026, the second-highest enrollment in the University’s 140-year history and set an all-time high for graduate enrollment.
 Graduate enrollment reached 1,749 students, a 5% increase over the previous record of 1,664 set last year. The graduate population includes more than 550 professional and research doctoral students, reflecting UTC’s expanding research enterprise and portfolio of advanced academic programs.
 “Our enrollment numbers show that the momentum at UTC continues,” said Chancellor Lori Bruce.

items.content_text:
The OECD unemployment rate was at 4.9% in July 2026, its lowest level in a year.
 The number of unemployed individuals in the OECD fell to 34.7 million, the lowest level in a year.
 In July 2026, unemployment rates remained steady at 6.1% in the European Union and 6.4% in the euro area.
 Japan, Mexico and Korea maintained unemployment rates below 3.0%, the lowest among OECD countries.
 By contrast, Finland and Spain reported double-digit unemployment rates, with Finland nearly 5.0 percentage points (p.p.) above its historic low from almost two decades ago.
 Learn more:  https://brnw.ch/21x5G3h | #OECDstats

YEARS IN THE MAKING: Congratulations to CFD Captain Skyler Phillips and many caring community partners on the grand opening of the Harvesting Inclusive Playground at Jack Benson Heritage Park!
 Captain Phillips spearheaded the project, which is now the largest fully accessible playground in the Chattanooga area. A custom farm-themed playground was designed with universal accessibility at its core, ensuring children of all physical abilities can play together without barriers.
 Designed for ages 2–12, the park features fully ramped play structures, wheelchair-accessible carousel elements, adaptive swings, sensory enrichment stations, and seamless rubber surfacing for barrier-free play.
 It’s a model project for excellence for other designs like it at other parks and playgrounds!

 What's happening: The City of Collegedale is working with the Hamilton County Regional Planning Agency (RPA) and the Chattanooga-Hamilton County/North Georgia Transportation Planning Organization (MPO) to gather data on how our community uses the greenway.

 We appreciate our residents helping make Collegedale an even more connected, walkable community! 
 Questions or concerns about the count period or device placement? Contact us at (423) 396-3135.

HCSO, TBI, Homeland Security Investigations Joint Investigation Unveils Local Business Was a Cover for a Prostitution Operation
 Hamilton County, TN – On the late morning of September 9, 2026, a joint undercover investigation involving the HCSO Criminal Investigations Unit, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI), and Homeland Security Investigations uncovered a woman soliciting prostitution at S-Lucky Spa, address 7794 East Brainerd Road, Suite 110. 
 The business was found on a website known for advertising prostitution, and an investigation into the business confirmed the spa was being used as a cover for prostitution. An undercover operation was conducted alongside the execution of a search warrant for the business. Authorities arrested a female employee, identified as Wei Guang Han, during the operation, and evidence identified as being used for the furtherance of crime to include money, was seized during the investigation.
 Han was transported to the Hamilton County Jail & Detention Center and faces the following charge: 
 • Prostitution
 Direct any questions to the TBI and Homeland Security Investigations. View the TBI's news release here: https://tbinewsroom.com/…/statewide-operation-addresses-il…/.

 Deputy Faulkner passed away on April 10, 2026, two days after his patrol vehicle collided with a disabled truck on a highway. Faulkner is remembered for his devotion to his family, dedication to law enforcement, and commitment to public service.

Today, Hamilton County EMS joins our nation in solemn remembrance of the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.
 Twenty-five years have passed, but we have not forgotten the 2,977 lives lost, including the firefighters, law enforcement officers, EMS professionals, and other first responders who answered the call that morning—many making the ultimate sacrifice while trying to save others.
 We remember the courage displayed in the face of unimaginable tragedy. We remember the families whose lives were forever changed. And we honor those who continued to serve in the days, months, and years that followed, many suffering lasting effects from their service at Ground Zero.
 For those of us in emergency services, September 11 remains a powerful reminder of what it means to answer the call—to run toward those who need us when others are running away.
 On this 25th anniversary, the men and women of Hamilton County EMS pause to remember, honor, and reflect.
 May we never forget September 11, 2001. 
 343 Firefighters.
 37 Port Authority Police Officers.
 23 NYPD Officers.
 8 EMS Professionals.
 And thousands of innocent lives.
 We will never forget.

Join us. Ceremony ribbon cutting at 10 followed by opening of the playground. 
 Harvest Inclusive Play, featuring two distinct playgrounds, is the largest fully accessible play space in Hamilton County. Designed for people of all abilities to play side by side, it expands recreational access for the entire community. The facility includes a 6,000-square-foot playground tailored for children ages 2–5, the only municipal inclusive playground for this age group in the county—and an 11,000-square-foot playground for ages 5–12. This thoughtful separation lets younger children enjoy appropriately sized equipment while keeping the environment safe and engaging for everyone.

UPDATE: CPD Makes Arrest in Tunnel Blvd Shooting
 CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. -- The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) has arrested a suspect in the shooting on Tunnel Boulevard that occurred on September 7, 2026. Devonta Shepherd (DOB: 11/03/94) was taken into custody and transported to the Hamilton County Jail and Detention Center. He is charged with Attempted 1st Degree Murder, Aggravated Assault, Unlawful Possession (Felon), and Employing a Firearm During the Commission of a Dangerous Felony.
 The information is preliminary and is subject to change as the investigation continues. Chattanooga Police ask anyone with information regarding this incident to call 423-698-2525.
 The charges and allegations referenced in this release are merely accusations of criminal conduct and not evidence. A defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt and convicted through due process of law.
 ###
 Original Release:
 CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. – The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) is investigating a shooting that occurred at approximately 09:45 a.m. in the 400 block of Tunnel Blvd.
 Officers responded to a report of a person being shot. Upon arrival, officers located a 41-year-old male with a gunshot wound. Officers rendered medical aid before EMS transported the victim to a local hospital for a potentially non-life-threatening injury.
 CPD Homicide and Crime Scene Units responded to investigate and process the scene. No suspect information is currently available.
 This information is preliminary and subject to change as the investigation continues. Chattanooga Police ask anyone with information regarding this incident to call 423-698-2525.
 #CPDnews

A collaboration of researchers from UTC and Marmara University in Türkiye has received a U.S. design patent for a wearable device designed for people with essential tremor—a neurological movement disorder that can make routine tasks such as writing, eating, drinking, dressing and using a computer more difficult.
 The patent covers the ornamental design for an upper-extremity tremor control device developed through a partnership that began nearly three years ago. The device fits around a user’s wrist and forearm and uses a modular design intended to accommodate different body sizes and needs.

Sheriff Austin Garrett and the men and women of the HCSO stand with the Knox County Sheriff’s Office as they mourn the passing of retired Sheriff Tom Spangler. 
 “Retired Sheriff Tom “Spanky” Spangler was a friend, a leader, a mentor, and the definition of strength and courage to me and many other law enforcement professionals across our great state. He served Knox County with true servant leadership, and his passing is a tremendous loss not only to Knox County but to every sheriff in this state; my prayers and condolences go to the Spangler family and his KCSO family. We will see you on the other side, my friend,” stated Sheriff Austin Garrett. 
 Please join us in keeping Sheriff Spangler’s family, friends, and colleagues, and Knox County in our thoughts and prayers during this difficult time.

items.content_text: Today marks 25 years since the 9/11 terrorist attack. A day that changed our country forever. A day when we lost nearly 3,000 lives. A day when first responders embodied bravery, running toward danger without hesitation. A day that brought unimaginable grief to Americans, and proved this country's resilience. Today we pause to remember those we lost, the survivors, and the courageous first responders who continue to inspire us now.
